currentUserGoal: Fix hard-to-read text on the class select screen and do a quick readability pass on the rest of the visible UI.
changesMade: Improved class select text rendering by using higher-resolution Phaser text textures for the class picker text objects.
Increased contrast for class picker subtitles, card metadata, passive summaries, descriptions, compact ability text, and buttons.
Stopped the two-row class picker from vertically crushing full description cards in screenshot-sized desktop/tablet layouts.
Changed short landscape class picker layouts to use the existing compact details panel rather than compressed full cards.
Reset full-card word wrapping after resizing back from compact layouts so long class names and passive names do not remain wrapped.
Tightened three-stat class card body copy spacing so descriptions and stat lines do not collide with the Start buttons.

verificationRun.result: Passed after the initial readability patch.
Passed after the follow-up overlap/wrap fix.

verificationRun.method: Browser visual check via local Chrome against http://127.0.0.1:5173/
verificationRun.result: Passed visually. The screenshot-sized layout now shows full 2x2 cards without vertical text squashing or button overlap; short landscape and phone layouts use compact cards plus a readable details panel.

verificationRun.method: Browser visual readability sweep via local Chrome against http://127.0.0.1:5173/
verificationRun.result: No console warnings/errors. Main HUD, skill tree, quest log, store, and options read cleanly. Disabled seed/store copy is intentionally muted but still legible in the checked desktop view.
Only one literal 10px call remains, on the hidden body placeholder for compact class cards.

knownIssues: The in-app browser screenshot API timed out after viewport overrides during this session, so the visual screenshots were captured with the runtime Playwright library using the locally installed Chrome executable.
Disabled shop/store item text remains deliberately lower contrast. It passed the quick visual check, but a dedicated accessibility pass could tune disabled-state contrast more formally.
nextRecommendedSteps: Play the class picker once on an actual phone/tablet browser and judge whether the compact details panel feels large enough under touch.
If doing a broader UI accessibility pass later, start with disabled shop/store item contrast and small status labels rather than the main HUD or class picker.
doNotRevert: Do not bring back vertical scaling for full class cards in two-row desktop/tablet layouts.
Do not remove the compact class ability details panel unless replacing it with another tested touch-friendly way to inspect passives.
